metaData.originalTitle: How to Fine-Tune Nemotron 3.5 ASR for Your Language， Domain， or Accent
metaData.title: How to Fine-Tune Nemotron 3.5 ASR for Your Language， Domain， or Accent
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 ASR, a 600M-parameter streaming multilingual speech-to-text model, and provides a detailed, practical guide on how to fine-tune it for specific languages, domains, or accents.
metaData.summary: The article presents NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 ASR, a 600M-parameter streaming multilingual speech-to-text model that transcribes 40 language-locales in real time with built-in punctuation and capitalization. It addresses common pain points in multilingual ASR, such as the need for multiple models, the streaming-vs-accuracy tradeoff, and post-processing pipelines. The model uses a Cache-Aware FastConformer-RNNT architecture for low-latency streaming without accuracy loss. The second half of the article provides a step-by-step guide to fine-tuning the model, covering data preparation, training, evaluation, and deployment. A worked example on Greek and Bulgarian shows significant Word Error Rate reductions (32% and 31% respectively) after fine-tuning with a few thousand hours of data. The article concludes with use cases like voice agents, live multilingual captions, and call-center analytics.

mainPoints.point: Nemotron 3.5 ASR solves the polyglot tax by using a single model for 40 language-locales.
mainPoints.explanation: This eliminates the need to stitch together multiple models or vendor APIs, simplifying infrastructure and reducing complexity.

mainPoints.point: Its Cache-Aware FastConformer architecture achieves low latency without sacrificing accuracy.
mainPoints.explanation: By caching internal states, the model avoids redundant recomputation, enabling true streaming with minimal delay and high accuracy.

mainPoints.point: Fine-tuning is transformative for under-resourced languages and specialized domains.
mainPoints.explanation: A worked example on Greek and Bulgarian shows 31-32% relative WER improvement after fine-tuning with a few thousand hours of targeted data.

mainPoints.point: The fine-tuning recipe is practical and reproducible.
mainPoints.explanation: The article provides a clear five-step workflow (data, train, evaluate, scale, deploy) with a companion GitHub repo containing exact commands and configs.

mainPoints.point: Key lessons include evaluating at deployment latency and protecting other languages during fine-tuning.
mainPoints.explanation: The authors emphasize measuring on held-out data at the target latency and using replay data to avoid degrading performance on other languages.

keyQuotes: The model uses a Cache-Aware FastConformer-RNNT architecture that streams audio without the redundant recomputation that makes most streaming ASR slow --- so you get low latency *and* high accuracy, not one at the expense of the other.
Fine-tuning is transformative for under-resourced languages --- the biggest wins came where the base model was weakest.
Evaluate at deployment latency, on held-out data. Training-set scores flatter you; a separate test set at 0 ms look-ahead tells the truth.
